question.problem:
Consider the matrix $E=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].$ If $f(X)={X}^{2}+4X-5$, find $f(E).$
$f(E)=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}}
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}+4X-5 \\  & ={X}^{2}+4X-5I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(E)={E}^{2}+4E-5I.$

Let's calculate ${E}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}^{2} & =E\cdot E \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(E):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(E) & ={E}^{2}+4E-5I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]+4[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 4 & 4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4+8-5 & 0+0-0 \\ 3+4-0 & 1+4-5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
